implementation_notes: Kotlin absorbs the pattern into the language: the documentation states that a function marked with the tailrec modifier whose recursive call meets the formal conditions is compiled to a fast loop instead of using the stack, so the recursive formulation stays in the source and the frames never exist. The conditions are strict and part of the contract: the function must call itself as its final operation, it cannot do so inside try/catch/finally blocks, and an open function cannot be tailrec - which also rules out mutual recursion. Write the tailrec function when the recursive shape is the clearest formulation; fall back to an explicit loop when the conditions cannot be met.
idiom_name: tailrec modifier (compiler rewrites the call into a loop)
pitfalls: tailrec covers self-recursion only: a mutually recursive pair compiles to ordinary calls and still overflows, so use a loop or a trampoline for even/odd-style pairs.
The call must be the final operation: wrapping it in try, runCatching or a post-processing expression loses the optimization even though the source still looks recursive.
An open function or an interface implementation cannot carry tailrec, which pushes the iteration back into the caller's loop.
